source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public Deuteronomy 29:1 binds Hebrew 28:69; public 29:2–29 binds Hebrew 29:1–28. All other public verses in chapters 27–34 align directly. All 266 original XML records, including written/read and numbering notes, are hashed in full.

key_decisions.decision: Preserves the elliptical not-his-children and blemish clauses without adding an unsupported temporal no longer.
Uses created for the acquire/create verb while retaining fatherhood and the other two making verbs.
Follows pinned children of Israel rather than importing sons of God; retains Adam and inheritance imagery.
Follows the recorded read form for heights and preserves the striking suckling-from-rock images.
Keeps the complete food list, shifts to you, and blood-of-grapes image; renders wheat-kidney fat idiom in the text and explains it in a note.
Retains Jeshurun, the abrupt you/he movement, and the contrast between nourishment and abandonment.
Retains both fathering and birth-labor imagery for God instead of harmonizing them to a single parental image.
Preserves the no-god/no-people and jealousy/anger reversals without importing a later identity for the nation.
Preserves hunger, two disease forces, wild teeth, and crawling venom while avoiding certainty about obscure disease names.
Selects scatter for the rare disputed verb and retains the stated intent to erase human remembrance.
Keeps the difficult divine feared language and the enemies’ denial of divine agency, then closes this speech.
Leaves they unidentified because the song’s movement between Israel and enemies is consequentially ambiguous.
Keeps the exact numerical pairs and the divine selling and handing-over images.
Marks renewed divine first-person speech without adding an otherwise absent reporting clause.
Chooses vindicate and compassion in context while retaining the uncertain confined/free totality formula.
Retains emphatic repeated I and both opposed pairs under a single divine agent.
Retains personified weapons, captive victims, and the difficult long-haired-head reading with alternatives noted.
Follows the shorter pinned stanza; supplies with for the compact opening and preserves land/people in the atonement close.
Keeps the pinned name Hoshea rather than silently harmonizing it to Joshua.
Preserves the imperative force and repeated gathering-to-people idiom, including Aaron and Hor.
